transcript: Pulitzer Prize-winning English by Sanaz Toossi is currently in previews on Broadway. Set in a 2008 classroom in Iran, a small group of people are learning English and studying for the TOEFL. This is a play about communication, assimilation, and the inextricable relationships between language and identity. The classroom setting provides a sandbox for the characters to explore and stumble through their learning process, which brings a lot of humor that anyone who's ever tried to learn another language could relate to. But the stringency of the “English only” rule set by the instructor also creates frustrations and surfaces some insecurities and resentment that can come with not being able to fully express oneself, and not just a lexical way. There's also definitely some underlying critiques here on how language in general and one's level of English proficiency can bring a whole slew of assumptions about them in certain settings. Overall, I thought this was a rich and layered play that captures universal aspects of communication through a specific and well-rendered lens. I would definitely recommend it. With that, another program for my collection.
